attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 15 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on RHEL9. Built a dedicated CA on node1, issued per-node server certs (with SAN) and a replicator client cert (CN=replicator), distributed via SSH. All three nodes run PostgreSQL with ssl=on and the CA as trust root. pg_hba.conf on every node restricts the `replication` database to `hostssl ... cert clientcert=verify-full` for the `replicator` role from the cluster subnet, with an explicit `hostnossl replication all reject` fallback, so only TLS connections presenting a certificate issued by this CA are accepted. Standbys were bootstrapped via pg_basebackup -R over verify-full mutual TLS, producing correct primary_conninfo with sslmode=verify-full and the client cert/key. Verified: (a) replication streams over TLS 1.3 with client cert CN=replicator recognized, (b) writes on node1 replicate to node2/node3, (c) a request without a client cert is rejected ('connection requires a valid client certificate'), (d) a cert signed by a different, untrusted CA is rejected at the TLS handshake ('unknown ca'), (e) plaintext replication attempts are rejected by pg_hba. Then executed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured a boot-id baseline and healthy replication baseline on all 3 nodes, restarted node2 then node3 (standbys) and finally node1 (primary) one at a time via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed PostgreSQL, recovery status, replication streaming (still TLS-encrypted with correct cipher), and full data consistency recovered on each node before moving to the next.
